profile.name: Pradyum Mistry
profile.whoami: Pradyum Mistry - Full Stack Developer, Game Developer, App Developer, Competitive Programmer, and AI/ML Enthusiast.
profile.about: I'm a Computer Engineering student at K. J. Somaiya School of Engineering who builds across the stack: production tooling at Barclays, on-device ML for accessibility, a self-hosted deployment platform, cross-chain smart contracts, and, since 2016, my own indie game studio, whose horror games have been played on YouTube by Markiplier and Jacksepticeye. I like hard problems with a visible payoff.
profile.currently: Ex-SWE Intern @ Barclays · B.Tech CE @ KJSSE '27

education.degree: B.Tech in Computer Engineering, Honours in Software and Mobile App Development
education.institution: K. J. Somaiya School of Engineering, Somaiya Vidyavihar University

bullets: Cut change-request turnaround from days to minutes for a 1.17M-row PostgreSQL table by building audited React/FastAPI CRUD tooling with server-side pagination, search and SQL trigger-based audit trails.

Built a graph-based task execution engine that runs dependent data loads with prerequisite handling and REST status tracking, plus a Kafka publishing utility that validates CSV, JSON and plain-text input before publishing.
Generated React forms at runtime from JSON schemas to trigger workflows, using events parsed from legacy HTML pages.
Shipped the tools as secure self-service apps with SSO, Docker and AWS, running on live data.
Optimised mixed-reality features in Unity and fixed XR module bugs, contributing to a 30% drop in crash rates.
Built a game for the 8th Wall Forge the Future Game Jam that won the “Most Addictive Game” award.
Started the studio in 2016 and have run it on my own since: 22 titles on itch.io, plus releases on Steam and Google Play, with 100,000+ downloads in total.
Signed a publishing deal with Upscale Studio to port Captive, a 3D horror game, to Nintendo.
Own the full pipeline: game design, C# and C++ gameplay code in Unity and Unreal Engine, builds for PC, web and Android, store pages, pricing and patches based on player feedback.
Games played on YouTube by Markiplier and Jacksepticeye, two creators with over 30M subscribers each.
Mentored the student team that won Realms, the hackathon hosted by Team Vision.
Ran AR/VR workshops and training sessions for members and led the club's technical projects.
Designed and maintained the club's website.

caseStudies.name: PRAMAN
caseStudies.tagline: An authorisation layer that lets AI shopping agents pay merchants safely
bullets: A 12-rule deterministic gate with no LLM in the payment path, paying merchants on Razorpay (test mode) and logging every decision to a hash-chained ledger that exports as a dispute pack.
Gemini 2.5 Flash turns photos of handwritten price lists into a store catalog, holding back low-confidence items before the store goes live; agents connect over an MCP server.
A 200-session harness (benign, prompt injection, replay, identity spoofing): the gate stopped all 65 bad transactions with no legitimate order blocked, at 3.6 ms p50. Backed by 312 tests.

caseStudies.name: Tugboat
bullets: Every git push is built into a container with Cloud Native Buildpacks (no Dockerfile), routed by Traefik and given a public HTTPS preview link.
Merges to main reach production through a health-checked blue-green swap, verified in tests with zero dropped requests, with one-click rollback.

Control plane with GitHub OAuth, HMAC-verified webhooks, live build logs and per-project env vars and CPU/memory limits, tested end to end against real Docker, Traefik, GitHub and Cloudflare tunnels with no mocks.

caseStudies.name: NameGate
caseStudies.tagline: Tokenized bonds with ENSv2 subnames as an on-chain compliance layer
bullets: A permissionless beacon contract reads ENS records and relays KYC state cross-chain over Chainlink CCIP, instead of an off-chain database.
194 tests, including 49 live tests on Sepolia and Hedera testnet, which caught an 8- vs 18-decimal mismatch between HBAR and its EVM representation.

caseStudies.name: Project Wayfinder
caseStudies.tagline: An offline phone app for blind and deaf users
bullets: Combines obstacle detection, depth estimation and sign language in one hardware-free, fully offline app.
20+ FPS on-device obstacle detection over a 20 m range by combining YOLO boxes with MiDaS depth maps and prioritised text-to-speech alerts.
Trained and compared 13 YOLO models (v10n, 11s, 26s) on a 7-class COCO + Kaggle dataset; best mAP50-95 0.576.

caseStudies.name: Milan
caseStudies.tagline: Indian Sign Language learning app, live on Google Play
bullets: ISLRTC-verified sign dictionary, lessons, real-time practice feedback and daily streaks.
98%+ gesture recognition with two models on MediaPipe hand landmarks: Dynamic Time Warping for moving signs and a Random Forest for static ones, running offline with TFLite.

caseStudies.name: SkillVersus
caseStudies.tagline: Real-time 1v1 coding duels, contests and typing battles
bullets: Run in a college lab with 24 concurrent users.
Socket.io and Redis for matchmaking and live match state, Judge0 for sandboxed multi-language execution, a 5-tier ranking, and fullscreen and tab-switch checks against cheating.
